findings.title: Date-override availability does not require the whole event to fit in the override
findings.body: The override check only rejects a slot whose end is at/before the override start or whose start is after the override end. It never rejects a slot that starts within the override but ends after its end (and also permits a slot that begins before the override and crosses its start). For example, with a 10:00-11:00 override and a 60-minute event, a 10:30 slot is considered available even though the host is only available until 11:00. This can advertise and book fixed hosts outside their date override.

findings.title: Fixed-host working hours are compared against UTC slot clock values
findings.body: `slotStartTime` is explicitly converted to UTC, but its UTC weekday/hour/minutes are compared directly with `workingHour.days`, `startTime`, and `endTime`, which represent the host schedule's local clock values. `organizerTimeZone` is not used for this working-hours comparison. A fixed host in a non-UTC timezone can therefore pass or fail the new fixed-host availability filter at the wrong local time; for example, a UTC+05:30 host's 18:00 local boundary is checked as 12:30 against an 18:00 local end. The check also sets `end` equal to the slot start, so it does not verify that the event duration fits before the working-hours end. This can expose round-robin slots when a fixed host is unavailable.

findings.title: The added test does not cover fixed-host round-robin overrides
findings.body: The stated primary regression is a round-robin event with a fixed host, but the added test is a single-user event and only exercises slot generation. It never exercises `checkIfIsAvailable` for fixed hosts, where this PR adds the override and working-hours filtering. Consequently, regressions that still offer a round-robin slot while its fixed host is outside an override are not caught.
